$comment: The CARLA scene-graph compatibility contract.
Transcribed from the generator itself — carla_sgg/sgg.py (the base graph),
carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py::process_to_junction_rsv (the abstraction this
repository consumes) and carla_sgg/actors.py (the class maps). Every claim
below cites where it comes from. Do NOT amend this file from memory or by
analogy with another project's adapter: it is the input a plan agent uses to
decide whether a law can be formalized at all, and a wrong entry here
silently converts a formalizable law into an `unsupported` one.
outside Tier A is hard-failed by tools/check_spec.py because it could never
Tier A is what the pipeline can produce at all; a spec referencing anything
outside Tier A is hard-failed by tools/check_spec.py because it could never
fire on real data.
The four availability tiers below are the important part:
attribute_keys        - readable from a rule today
partially_available   - the concept is reachable, with a stated residue
available_not_exposed - in the captured data, not yet lifted; this is a
vocabulary/adapter gap you may ASK for, not a
reason to declare a law unsupported
unavailable           - genuinely absent from the graph; the only tier
that justifies `unsupported`

provenance.generator: less-lab-uva/carla_scene_graphs (GPL-3.0; read for schema facts only, no code copied)
provenance.why_that_one: It is the only abstraction whose node naming (`Lane <road>_<±lane>`, `Road <n>`, `Junction <n>`, `Off Road`), `special_class` attribute and entity→lane→road→junction `isIn` chain match this library. `process_to_rsv` names lanes `Ego Lane` / `Left 1 of Ego Lane` / `Opposing Lane 0` / `Root Road` instead, which carla/adapter.py would classify as `other`, silently making every lane predicate false.
provenance.ego_log: capture_sensor_data.py and sg/carla_scene_graphs/src/carlaspec/runner.py both write ego_logs.json: one record per frame with state.velocity/acceleration/transform/angular_velocity and control.throttle/brake/steer/gear/hand_brake/reverse. Indexed by absolute capture frame — a converted window must offset into it.

time_base.how_to_use: A statutory duration becomes a frame count: `TrafficSpec.secondsToFrames 1 = 20`. State the assumed rate in the rule. This is a modelling assumption, not a missing field — a capture that saved every tick has exactly 50 ms frames.

entity_types.$comment: These are the Lean `EntityType` constructors verbatim — write `.car`, not `.vehicle_car`. Each corresponds to a base class from actors.py::get_base_type, or to a structure node process_to_junction_rsv creates.

notes.van: CARLA's ambulance (`vehicle.ford.ambulance`) and sprinter are vans. NO proximity or angular edge is ever emitted for a van — see relation_coverage.
notes.vehicle: Base class for CARLA's single old `Vehicles` semantic label, which IS excluded from the proximity tables. Do not read this as 'background vehicles are excluded' — see static_background_vehicles.
notes.trafficLight: MEASURED: one node per traffic-light ACTOR, not per light box. sgg.py tries `actor.get_light_boxes()` first but that block raises AttributeError on CARLA 0.9.16 and the `except` fallback (sgg.py:613) runs instead, emitting one node carrying only `carla_id` and `carla_type_id` plus `light_state`. `carla_parent_id`, `carla_semantic_tags`, `carla_actor_state` and `carla_attr` are set only by the branch that does not run, so they never reach a capture (0 occurrences in 480 frames). A junction still contributes several traffic-light entities, one per approach.
notes.speedLimitSign: `traffic.speed_limit.<kph>` actor. Carries the posted value but NO `controls` edge.
notes.landmark: The map's own OpenDRIVE sign record, linked to lanes by `mayAffect`. This is the authoritative source for posted restrictions.
notes.junctionBoundary: Only present if the map was initialised with `init_to_world(parse_junction_boundaries=True)`; the default is False, so treat it as absent unless the capture says otherwise.
notes.lane: One node per (junction, road, lane) triple. All waypoint-level attributes are dropped; only the name survives.
notes.offRoad: The single `Off Road` node. Every actor with no driving-lane edge is `isIn` it — pedestrians on the pavement included, because sidewalk nodes are filtered out.
notes.other: Anything carla/adapter.py could not classify. A rule should never bind this.
notes.absent_on_purpose: `Sidewalk` nodes and any blueprint for which get_base_type returns None (`traffic.unknown`, `static.prop`, `CityObjectLabel.*` background props) never reach the RSV graph.
notes.static_background_vehicles:
MEASURED, and a trap. `sgg.py` Step 4 ("add static vehicles", ~line 411) ingests the map's PARKED-CAR LEVEL GEOMETRY via `world.get_environment_objects(CityObjectLabel.Car/Bus/Truck/Bicycle/Motorcycle)` and names each node with the enum string as `sem_class` ('Car', 'Bus', ...). `actors.py::base_type_map` maps those strings to the REAL base classes ('Car'->'car', 'Bus'->'bus', 'Truck'->'truck', 'Bicycle'->'bicycle', 'Motorcycle'->'motorcycle') — every one of which IS in DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS. So parked scenery becomes a `.car` entity with the same proximity and angular edges as moving traffic, and Lean cannot tell them apart: same EntityType, same bands, same `special_class` ('').
Distinguishing marks in the captured data: `carla_id` and `carla_type_id` are ABSENT (a real actor has both), `entity_id` is negative, `sem_class` is the capitalised label rather than a `vehicle.*` blueprint id, and the node has NO `isIn` edge to any driving lane.
Consequence 1 — grounding inflation: `vehicleBinder` and `proximityVehicleBinder` ground on parked scenery. Measured on capture `max_speed_violation`, which contains ZERO real vehicle actors: two static `car_*` nodes at 16-31 m for 40 frames, and every two-binder vehicle rule grounded 6 times. That inflates the count `scripts/capture_eval.py` uses to decide whether a law was engaged.
Consequence 2 — a false-positive risk that is currently masked: every distance-using rule in the library also requires `Pred.sameLane` or `Pred.isEmergency`, and a static node satisfies neither (no lane edge, empty special_class). That is luck, not a guarantee. A rule of the form 'do not pass within N metres of a cyclist', which needs a band and an angular edge but no shared lane, would convict lawful driving past a parked bicycle. If a rule needs a distance WITHOUT a lane test, gate it on evidence of a real actor.

relation_labels.$comment: Lean `RelLabel` constructors verbatim. `inFrontOf` and `behind` are NOT labels — they are Pred-level disjunctions over the direct/side split.

notes.safety_hazard_spelling: The generator's code emits `safety_hazard` (DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_THRESHOLDS) while its own docs/Abstractions.md says `safe_hazard`. The adapter accepts both; one that accepts only the documented spelling drops every closest-band edge.
notes.band_names_are_not_english: `safetyHazard` is the CLOSEST band (<2 m) and `near` is the second FARTHEST (10-16 m). Exactly one band is emitted per pair. Always use `Pred.withinMetres`, which takes the union of every band at or below the bound.
notes.controls_is_the_only_governance_edge: `controlsTrafficOf` is built from a traffic light's affected lane waypoints (sgg.py:628, `actor.get_affected_lane_waypoints()`) and from a stop sign's trigger volume (sgg.py:676). CRITICAL, MEASURED: every waypoint `get_affected_lane_waypoints()` returns is INSIDE the junction (Town03: 112 junction, 0 non-junction), so every `controls` edge from a traffic light targets a junction-internal lane (2635 of 2635 edges across two captures). `Pred.governs d v` therefore ENTAILS `Pred.inAnyJunction v`, which makes `governs d v ⋀ ¬ₛ inAnyJunction v` — the natural reading of 'facing a red before entering' — UNSATISFIABLE on generator output. Rules/Signal/R0004 has that shape and its antecedent held on 0 of 240 frames of a capture where the ego demonstrably ran a red light. CARLA exposes the approach-lane association as `TrafficLight.get_stop_waypoints()` (Town03: 49 non-junction waypoints) but the generator never calls it, so it is absent from every capture. A stop sign's trigger volume sits on the approach, so `facingStopSign` may not have this problem — UNVERIFIED, no capture yet contains a stop-sign controls edge.
notes.isIn_from_a_sign_is_not_governance: Every actor gets `isIn` edges to the driving nodes its bounding box overlaps (sgg.py::__add_to_graph), signs included. A sign's `isIn` therefore matches the sign facing the cross street just as well; it is a weak proxy.
notes.isIn_is_overloaded: entity→lane, lane→road, road→junction all use `isIn`. Query it type-filtered (`Scene.relatedToTyped`, or the typed predicates in Core/Vocab.lean).

relation_coverage.$comment: WHICH PAIRS the distance and angular edges are actually emitted for. This is the single most common source of a spec that compiles, passes its hand-written scenarios, and can never fire on a capture.

proximity_and_angular_pairs.rule: Emitted only for ordered pairs matching DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS / DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_RELATIONS, every entry of which pairs the base class `ego` with one other base class.
proximity_and_angular_pairs.ego_is_always_one_end: There is NEVER a proximity or angular edge between two non-ego actors. A two-vehicle rule must bind the ego vehicle as one of the two, or it grounds and is trivially satisfied forever.

excluded_and_why.van: not listed in DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS at all
excluded_and_why.traffic_light: the table spells it `traffic light` (space) while the base class is `traffic_light` (underscore), so the equality test never matches
excluded_and_why.stop_sign: the table spells it `stop sign` while the base class is `stop_sign`

proximity_and_angular_pairs.consequence: No distance to any sign or signal exists. Use `controls` / `mayAffect`. And a rule about an emergency vehicle plus a distance can only ground on the police car (`car`) and the firetruck (`truck`), never the ambulance (`van`).
proximity_and_angular_pairs.lean_binders: Core/Scene.lean::proximityTypes is this list verbatim; proximityVehicleTypes is its vehicle subset (bicycle, car, truck, bus, motorcycle). Use proximityVehicleBinder / proximityRoadUserBinder for any rule needing a distance. roadUserTypes and vehicleTypes admit `van` and `vehicle`, which carry no proximity edge: binding them grounds and can never report a violation.

inter_lane_edges.rule: `opposes`, `toLeftOf` and `toRightOf` between lane nodes are emitted only for ADJACENT lane ids of the same road (`zip(sorted_lanes, sorted_lanes[1:])`).
inter_lane_edges.consequence: Two lanes separated by a third carry none of these labels, and lanes of different roads are never related this way.

entity_presence.render_distance: Only nodes inside the ego's render bbox (default 50 m forward) are in a frame.
entity_presence.occlusion: With `check_occlusion=True`, actors the ego cannot see are omitted entirely.
entity_presence.consequence: Absence of an entity is NOT evidence that it does not exist. Never write a rule whose violation depends on something not being in the graph.

attribute_keys.$comment: Readable from a rule today, via the Pred.attr* family. Anything not listed here is rejected by tools/check_spec.py.

sem_class.source: the CARLA blueprint / type id the generator copies into Node.attr

base_class.source: NOT read from the RSV graph, which carries no `base_class` key in node.attr (0 occurrences in 480 frames) — it lives on the Node object as a Python field. carla/adapter.py reads it there to choose the Lean EntityType, and Core/Builders.lean re-derives the attribute from that type via EntityType.baseClass. So it IS readable, with one exception: `mkEgo` hard-codes base_class = "ego", so the ego's value is "ego" and NOT "car". A rule writing `Pred.baseClass v "car"` to mean 'v is a car' silently excludes the ego.

special_class.source: actors.py::get_special_type; empty string when ordinary. Prefer Pred.isEgo / isEmergency

accel.source: ego_logs state.acceleration.value — the graph carries only the component vector carla_acc_x/y/z, whose magnitude would need a square root

at_traffic_light.source: carla_affected_by_traffic_light (ego.is_at_traffic_light()) — inside a governing signal's trigger volume, says nothing about its colour

light_brake.source: sgg.py: actor.get_light_state() unpacked per carla.VehicleLightState member. MEASURED: the ego is appended to `exclude_ids` in generate_graph_for_frame, so it never enters the actor loop and carries NO light_* attribute at all (0 occurrences on the ego node in 480 frames). `Pred.brakeLightOn v` is always false when v is the ego.

road_id.source: re-read from the node name by Core/Builders.lean

lane_id.source: re-read from the node name; sign is the OpenDRIVE side of the road reference line, negative right / positive left, and all lanes of one travel direction share a sign

posted_limit_kph.source: the trailing number of the blueprint id traffic.speed_limit.<kph>

landmark_type.meaning: OpenDRIVE type code: 274 speed limit, 206 stop, 205 give way

attribute_keys.decimal_note: Decimal and integer attributes are float- or int-formatted strings of arbitrary precision. Compare them with TrafficSpec.Pred.attrMilli* (milli-unit integer comparison; 1 m/s = 1000, and "-1" is -1000), never by string equality. Booleans are the literal strings "true" / "false"; read them with Pred.attrTrue, and note that an absent boolean reads as false, which is the correct default for a light that is off.
attribute_keys.no_float_ever: There is no Float anywhere in the library. Comparisons stay decidable and kernel-clean.

partially_available.$comment: The concept is reachable, but with a residue you must state in the rule's notes. This is the tier that most often gets misfiled as `unsupported`.

posted_speed_limit.available: OpenDRIVE landmarks (`landmark_type == "274"`, value in km/h) linked to lanes by `mayAffect`; plus `traffic.speed_limit.<kph>` sign actors carrying `posted_limit_kph`.
posted_speed_limit.residue: A landmark reaches the graph only if it is within the capture's render distance of a driving node, so its absence does not prove the road is unrestricted. The sign actors have no governance edge, only bounding-box `isIn`.

which_half_of_the_roadway.available: Lane-to-lane `toLeftOf` / `toRightOf`, each computed in the TARGET lane's own forward frame. That makes the edge pattern between two lanes reveal their relative direction of travel: asymmetric (`a toLeftOf b` with `b toRightOf a`) means same direction, mutual (`a toLeftOf b` and `b toLeftOf a`) means opposite, because each lane is judged from its own heading. So 'am I keeping right' is decidable relative to the vehicle's own direction of travel: a driver keeping right has no same-direction lane to the right.
which_half_of_the_roadway.residue: `inRightmostLane` is slightly stricter than the statutory 'right half': on a three-lane carriageway it demands the rightmost lane, not merely the right-hand half, so pair it with the statute's own overtaking or manoeuvring exception. It is also false for a vehicle occupying no lane at all, which is why `hasLaneToTheRight` exists as the positive form.
which_half_of_the_roadway.do_not_use: The `lane_id` SIGN (Pred.laneRightOfReference / laneLeftOfReference / inLaneRightOfReference / inLaneLeftOfReference). It records which side of the OpenDRIVE reference line a lane was authored on, not a legal side of the road: every lane of one direction of travel shares the sign, so the lawful carriageway of a divided road, or a one-way street the map numbers positively, is entirely `left of reference`. A rule built on it reports a violation on every frame of lawful driving there. This was measured, not predicted: rule `Lane/R0009` formalized 'the right half of the roadway' that way, passed all four of its own scenarios, and then convicted 50 frames of compliant driving in the bundled sceneflow capture.

wrong_way_driving.available: Two routes. (1) Relative heading: the angular edges are computed from the source actor's forward vector, so two actors are mutually `inFrontOf` exactly when their headings differ by more than 90° — an oncoming pair. (2) Lane connectivity over time: if v is in l1 now and in l2 next frame while the graph says `l2 travelsTo l1`, v moved against the lane's direction of travel.
wrong_way_driving.residue: Route (1) is symmetric — it establishes that a pair is converging, not which one is misplaced. Route (2) needs the vehicle to actually change lane node between frames, and only the ego reliably has the lane membership to observe it.

stop_before_intersection.available: `stopped` (ego speed ≤ 0.1 m/s), `inAnyJunction` / `inJunction`, `approachingJunction` (lane `travelsTo` a junction lane), and `facingStopSign` via the `controls` edge.
stop_before_intersection.residue: There is no stop-line position, so 'before entering' becomes 'while approaching and not yet in the junction'. The duration becomes a frame count at 20 Hz.
stop_before_intersection.vocabulary: Pred.stopped / facingStopSign / approachingJunction / inAnyJunction, plus TrafficSpec.secondsToFrames

another_vehicle_braking_or_signalling.residue: A light is evidence of the driver's action, not of the resulting motion, and stays false if the simulated traffic manager never actuates it — check the grounding count on a real capture.

pedestrian_off_the_carriageway.available: A pedestrian with no driving-lane edge is `isIn` the `Off Road` node (`Pred.offRoadway`).
pedestrian_off_the_carriageway.residue: Sidewalk nodes are filtered out by process_to_junction_rsv, so pavement, verge and central reservation are indistinguishable from each other.

signal_change_event.available: A change of `light_state` between adjacent frames — a temporal formula, no extra field needed.
signal_change_event.residue: Frame granularity is 50 ms; a change is only observed if both frames were captured.

available_not_exposed.$comment: Present in the captured data, not yet lifted into Lean by carla/adapter.py. A law needing one of these is NOT unsupported — it is blocked on a vocabulary/adapter extension, which you should request explicitly in the plan rather than recording the law as unsupported. Extending it means changing carla/adapter.py, Core/Vocab.lean and this file together.
available_not_exposed.actor_geometry: Every actor node carries `vertex` (x,y,z) and unit `forward` / `right` / `up` vectors (sgg.py::__add_to_graph). Not lifted because exact distances and absolute headings need square roots and pairwise arithmetic, which the milli-unit Int model does not provide; squared-distance comparisons would be the decidable way in.
available_not_exposed.ego_transform: ego_logs.json carries per-frame `state.transform` (x, y, z, pitch, yaw, roll) and the full velocity/acceleration/angular_velocity vectors. Only the scalar channels are lifted.
available_not_exposed.carla_identity: `carla_id`, `carla_type_id`, `carla_semantic_tags`, `carla_actor_state`, `carla_attr` on each actor — stable cross-frame identity and the exact blueprint attributes.
available_not_exposed.vehicle_light_state_raw: The packed `vehicle_light_state` integer, alongside the per-light booleans that are lifted.
available_not_exposed.waypoint_detail_needs_a_different_abstra: Lane width, both lane markings (colour / type / width / lane_change), `waypoint_s`, `is_junction`, `angle` and `curve` exist on the BASE graph's waypoint nodes, but process_to_junction_rsv collapses each waypoint run into one lane node carrying only a name. Reaching them means capturing a different abstraction, not just extending the adapter.

unavailable.$comment: Genuinely absent. This is the ONLY tier that justifies recording a law as `unsupported`, and the note must name the key. Before adding an entry here, find the line in carla_sgg/ that would have produced it and confirm it does not exist.
unavailable.non_ego_dynamics: speed / accel / throttle / brake / steer / yaw_rate / hand_brake / reverse exist for the ego vehicle only: copy_carla_actor_state and copy_carla_control are called for the ego node alone. Another vehicle's motion is observable only through its light states and through its proximity band changing across frames.
unavailable.exact_distance: Proximity is quantised into the six bands above. The base graph puts a metric `distance` on each edge, but process_to_junction_rsv does not copy it, so no numeric separation is recoverable.
unavailable.heading_relative_to_lane: The abstraction keeps no direction vector for a lane node, so a vehicle's absolute heading cannot be compared with the lane it occupies. Relative heading between two actors IS recoverable — see partially_available.wrong_way_driving.
unavailable.lane_width_and_markings: Collapsed away with the waypoint nodes; there is no carriageway width, no lane-marking type and no kerb.
unavailable.stop_line_and_junction_geometry: No coordinates survive for structure nodes, so a stop line, a give-way line, a crossing and a junction boundary have no position to test against.
unavailable.right_of_way: No explicit priority or right-of-way annotation. Signals and stop signs give de facto priority; otherwise derive it from occupancy order.
unavailable.timestamps: No frame carries a clock. Durations must become frame counts — see time_base.
unavailable.sidewalk_context: process_to_junction_rsv filters out `Sidewalk` nodes, so everything off the carriageway collapses into one `Off Road` node.
unavailable.environment: No weather, time of day, road-surface or visibility state anywhere in the graph.
unavailable.occupants_and_load: No occupancy, seatbelt, cargo, mass or dimension data.
unavailable.traffic_light_grouping: `carla_parent_id` would tie the light boxes of one junction to a parent signal, but sgg.py sets it only in the get_light_boxes() branch, which raises on CARLA 0.9.16; the fallback branch that actually runs does not. MEASURED absent from every traffic-light node in 480 frames, and `actor.parent` is None for lights in any case. No adapter change can lift it — it is not captured.

pitfalls: A vocabulary gap is not a data gap. If the field exists but no predicate reads it, request the predicate — do not record the law as `unsupported`.

A map convention is not a legal fact. OpenDRIVE lane-id signs, road ids and junction ids describe how the map was authored, not what a driver is permitted to do. Where a statute talks about sides, edges or directions, prefer a predicate defined relative to the vehicle's own direction of travel. Picking the predicate whose NAME matches the statute's words is how `Lane/R0009` came to convict 50 frames of lawful driving.

A rule that passes all of its own scenarios can still be wrong on every real capture, because the same reasoning wrote the formula and the scenarios. `run_spec monitor` against a human-labelled capture is the only check that is independent of it — assume any rule it has not seen is unvalidated.
Cite the generator, not this file's history. Every availability claim above names a file and a mechanism; if you believe something else is true, find the line.
No proximity or angular edge exists between two non-ego actors, or to any sign or signal, or to a van. Check relation_coverage before writing an antecedent that needs a distance.
`safetyHazard` is the closest band and `near` is nearly the farthest. Use Pred.withinMetres.
Relation direction reads 'src is <rel> tgt': `Pred.behind v w` means v is behind w, so in a following rule v is the follower. Inverting this silently reverses the rule.
Ego-only channels on a non-ego binder are silently false, which makes the whole antecedent false and the rule vacuously true.
A sign's `isIn` edge is bounding-box overlap, not governance. Use `controls` (lights, stop signs) or `mayAffect` (landmarks).
Absence of an entity is not evidence of absence in the world: render distance and occlusion filtering both drop entities.
Inter-lane `opposes` / `toLeftOf` / `toRightOf` only relate ADJACENT lane ids of the same road.
Two RSV nodes that happen to share a name collapse into one entity in carla/adapter.py, which keys entities by name.
Every rule needs a positive and a negative scenario, and every binder needs a distinct entity in every scenario trace, or the rule grounds zero times and tests nothing.

A rule's verdict must not depend on how long the capture is. Core/Semantics.lean::loopBounded reads a `.bounded n` window that overruns the trace as false, so `□ (¬ₛ .bounded n bad)` reports compliant on any trace shorter than n, with groundings >= 1 so the vacuity guard misses it. Measured on R0011 (n=80): 80 frames of an every-frame violation report false, 79 report true. Core/Formula.lean::SFProp.frameSpan computes the requirement and check_spec rejects short scenario traces as TRACE_TOO_SHORT.

The last n-1 frames of any trace are a blind zone for a `.bounded n` rule: a violation confined to them cannot be reported. Measured: 79 violating frames at the end of a 200-frame trace read as compliant.

Every binder MULTIPLIES the grounding count, and a binder over a structural type (lane, road) multiplies it by tens. `laneBinder "a", laneBinder "b"` is ~1,200 lane pairs on a real capture, of which only the pairs joined by an actual edge do any work — the rest make the antecedent false and are vacuously satisfied, so they cost a full trace evaluation each and contribute nothing. Prefer a predicate that quantifies lanes internally (`inRightmostLane`, `hasLaneToTheRight`, `laneTravelsTo` with `inLane`, `opposingLanes`): one scan per frame instead of a cross product. If the relation you need has no such predicate, request one rather than binding two lanes — see capture_reference_census.

recipes.$comment: Common statutory concepts and the construction that expresses them with today's vocabulary. Use these instead of re-deriving what is possible.
recipes.a vehicle is following another within N: Pred.followingWithin N v w — same lane, v behind w, band union at or below N. Bind the ego as one of the pair.
recipes.a driver faces a steady red signal: Pred.facingRedSignal v, or trafficLightBinder d + Pred.governs d v ⋀ Pred.signalRed d when the rule must name the signal. WARNING: both reduce to the same `controls` lookup, and that edge only exists once the vehicle is already inside the junction — see relation_labels.notes.controls_is_the_only_governance_edge. Do NOT conjoin either with `¬ₛ Pred.inAnyJunction v`: the conjunction is unsatisfiable on real captures and the rule will report compliant on every red-light runner.
recipes.the signal changed while the vehicle was: Pred.signalGreen d ⋀ Pred.inJunction v j at one position, then ◯ (Pred.signalRed d) — a temporal formula over light_state, no extra field.
recipes.a driver approaching a stop sign must st: Pred.facingStopSign v ⋀ Pred.approachingJunction v j ⋀ ¬ₛ Pred.inAnyJunction v, with .bounded (secondsToFrames 1) (Pred.stopped v) for the dwell, then Pred.inJunction v j. CAUTION: this is the same shape that makes R0004 unsatisfiable. A stop sign's `controls` edge comes from its trigger volume, which sits on the approach rather than inside the junction, so it probably survives — but that is UNVERIFIED against a capture. Check the grounding count.
recipes.not more than N km/h: Pred.speedLeKph v N (ego only). For a posted rather than a literal limit, Pred.withinPostedSpeedLimit v.
recipes.for at least one second: SFProp.bounded (TrafficSpec.secondsToFrames 1) φ — 20 frames at the reference capture rate. Record the assumption.
recipes.an oncoming vehicle is approaching in my: Pred.oncoming v w ⋀ Pred.sameLane v w, tightening bands across frames for 'approaching'.
recipes.a vehicle is driving against the flow: Pred.inLane v l₁ ⋀ ◯ (Pred.inLane v l₂) ⋀ Pred.laneTravelsTo l₂ l₁ — movement opposite to lane connectivity.
recipes.yield to an emergency vehicle: Pred.isEmergency w with a proximityVehicleBinder for w (an ambulance is a van and carries no distance edges), plus Pred.following / withinMetres.
recipes.the vehicle ahead is braking: Pred.brakeLightOn w — the only braking evidence for a non-ego vehicle.
recipes.the driver signalled before changing lan: Pred.rightBlinkerOn v (or left) at a position, then ◯ (Pred.inLane v l₂) with Pred.canLaneChangeTo l₁ l₂.
recipes.on the right-hand half of the roadway: Pred.inRightmostLane v, or ¬ₛ Pred.hasLaneToTheRight v when a vehicle off the roadway should not be convicted. Relative to the vehicle's own direction of travel, so no map convention is involved. Do NOT use the lane_id sign — see partially_available.which_half_of_the_roadway.do_not_use.
recipes.drive to the right-hand edge of the road: Same construction: Pred.inRightmostLane v. The graph has no kerb or carriageway edge, so 'the right-hand edge' degrades to 'the rightmost lane of my direction'; record that as the residue.
recipes.a duration in seconds: SFProp.bounded (TrafficSpec.secondsToFrames k) φ. The trace must be at least `SFProp.frameSpan` frames long or the rule reports compliant no matter what the trace contains — Core/Semantics.lean::loopBounded reads a window running off the end as false. Core/Grounding.lean publishes the span and tools/check_spec.py rejects short scenario traces with TRACE_TOO_SHORT.

capture_preconditions.$comment: Values this contract states as fact that are really CALLER-SUPPLIED DEFAULTS of the generator or the simulator. None of them is recorded in a capture, so nothing downstream can verify that the capture it is reading was made with them. They hold only for a capture recorded with generator defaults. A mismatch shifts every threshold silently, and because an unparseable or absent value makes both `leMilli` and `geMilli` false, the error direction is a MISSED violation.
capture_preconditions.capture_rate: time_base.capture_hz = 20 is world.settings.fixed_delta_seconds, chosen by the capture script (capture_sensor_data.py FPS=20; src/run_capture.py --fps). Core/Scene.lean freezes `captureHz := 20`, and time_base itself states that frames carry no timestamp — so the rate is unverifiable from the data by construction. At 40 Hz `secondsToFrames 1` = 20 frames means 0.5 s and a half-second rolling stop satisfies R0005.
capture_preconditions.proximity_band_metres: proximity_bands_closest_first is DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_THRESHOLDS, an overridable parameter of process_to_junction_rsv. The RSV keeps only the band LABEL, not the metres (verified: edge data keys are exactly {'label'}), so the mapping cannot be checked against a capture. Core/Scene.lean::distanceBands hard-codes it.
capture_preconditions.proximity_pair_table: relation_coverage is DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS / DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_RELATIONS, also overridable. 'ego is always one end' is a property of the default table.
capture_preconditions.directional_split_degrees: DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_THRESHOLDS (45/90/135). Pred.oncoming's 'headings differ by more than 90 degrees' depends on it.
capture_preconditions.segment_length: SGG(segment_length=1.0). NOT documented elsewhere in this file, though it sets lane-node granularity AND appears in the controls-edge test (`get_distance(...) < self.segment_length * 0.5`), so the governance edge R0004/R0005 depend on has a tolerance this contract never stated.
capture_preconditions.how_to_fix: Record the generator/simulator parameters alongside each capture and have carla/adapter.py hard-fail on disagreement with what Core assumes. Until then these are assumptions, not facts, and a plan agent should be told so.

capture_reference_census.$comment: How many DISTINCT entities of each binder type a real capture contains, measured on a 240-frame Town03 capture (red_light_compliant) with `traceEntityIds`. This is the basis for the grounding budget the gate enforces: `PropertySchema.bindings` is the cross product of these, so each extra binder MULTIPLIES the work, and a binder over a structural type multiplies it by a large number. Values below are rounded UP from the measurement to leave headroom for a busier capture — a budget check must not pass a rule that would then blow up on real traffic.
capture_reference_census.raw_measurement: vehicle 2 · lane 35 · road 23 · junction 2 · trafficLight 3 · stopSign 0 · landmark 3 · pedestrian 0
capture_reference_census.cost_per_grounding: Each grounding is one full `satisfies` over the whole trace. Measured: 16,637 groundings over 240 frames took 327 s of `lake env lean`, i.e. ~20 ms per grounding. Cost also grows with frames^2 because `Trace` is a `List Scene` and scene lookup is O(i).
capture_reference_census.why_it_bit: A 21-rule library in which 7 rules bound one or two LANES produced 8,775 to 16,637 groundings per capture and 239-327 s of evaluation, against a 300 s harness ceiling — so two of four captures were reported as unevaluable. Two captures with an identical 16,637 groundings landed on opposite sides of the ceiling, which is what a budget cliff looks like. The gate never saw it: a scenario trace holds 3-4 lanes, so the same rule grounds a handful of times there and passes in milliseconds.
